preconditions.description: The number of elements in set S is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= s <= 2 * 10**5 for s in S)
preconditions.description: All elements in S are distinct positive integers between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.
The set S contains exactly n distinct integers.

postconditions.description: The output x is a non-negative integer representing the largest possible exponent such that a magical permutation exists for integers from 0 to 2^x - 1.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= num <= 2**x - 1 for num in permutation)
postconditions.description: All elements in the permutation are integers from 0 to 2^x - 1 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all((permutation[i] ^ permutation[i+1]) in S for i in range(len(permutation)-1))
postconditions.description: The bitwise XOR of any two consecutive elements in the permutation is an element of S.

postconditions.expression: not any((2**(x+1) - 1) >= 0 and all((permutation[i] ^ permutation[i+1]) in S for i in range(len(permutation)-1)) for permutation in possible_permutations(2**(x+1)))
postconditions.description: No magical permutation exists for integers from 0 to 2^(x+1) - 1, ensuring x is the largest possible.
